CheckpointLoaderSimple.what: Opens a model file and hands out its three parts: the MODEL that draws, the CLIP that reads your words, and the VAE that turns pictures to and from latent space.
CheckpointLoaderSimple.why: It comes first because everything else needs one of its three parts. Follow its wires and you see who uses what.

UNETLoader.what: Loads just the drawing model (the diffusion model), without its text reader or VAE.
UNETLoader.why: Newer models ship as separate files, so the drawing part, the text part and the VAE each get their own loader.

CLIPLoader.what: Loads the text reader on its own.
CLIPLoader.why: Its CLIP goes to every Text Encode node.

DualCLIPLoader.what: Loads two text readers that work as a pair (Flux and SD3 use two).
DualCLIPLoader.why: Both read your prompt; the pair goes on to the Text Encode node.

VAELoader.what: Loads the VAE on its own: the translator between real pictures and latent space.
VAELoader.why: Anything that turns a picture into latents (encode) or latents back into a picture (decode) needs it.

LoraLoader.what: Adds a LoRA: a small add-on that teaches the model a face, a style or an object.
LoraLoader.why: It sits between the loader and the sampler, so the sampler gets the model with the LoRA already mixed in.

LoraLoaderModelOnly.what: Adds a LoRA to the drawing model only.
LoraLoaderModelOnly.why: Between the loader and the sampler, like any LoRA; this one leaves the text reader alone.

CLIPTextEncode.what: Turns your words into numbers the model understands (the conditioning).
CLIPTextEncode.why: Usually there are two: the positive prompt (what you want) and the negative prompt (what to avoid). Both wires end at the sampler.

CLIPSetLastLayer.what: Tells the text reader to stop a layer or two early, which some anime-style models expect.
CLIPSetLastLayer.why: Between the loader's CLIP and the Text Encode nodes.

ConditioningCombine.what: Joins two sets of prompt numbers into one.
ConditioningCombine.why: Used when a picture has several prompts at once; the joined result goes to the sampler.

EmptyLatentImage.what: Makes a blank canvas of noise in latent space at the size you ask for.
EmptyLatentImage.why: The sampler needs something to start from. For a brand-new picture that's empty noise; for editing a photo it's the photo, encoded.

EmptySD3LatentImage.what: A blank latent canvas sized for SD3 and Flux style models.
EmptySD3LatentImage.why: Same job as Empty Latent Image, for models that use a different latent shape.

KSampler.what: The artist. Starting from noise, it removes a little noise each step, guided by your prompt, until a picture appears. The step counter you see is this node working.
KSampler.why: Everything meets here: the MODEL from the loader, the positive and negative prompts, and the starting latent. Its result is still a latent, so a VAE Decode comes after.

KSamplerAdvanced.what: The sampler with more controls: start and stop at chosen steps, and add noise or not.
KSamplerAdvanced.why: Used for two-stage renders, where one sampler hands its half-finished picture to another.

SamplerCustomAdvanced.what: A sampler built from parts: a noise source, a guider, a sampler type and a schedule, each a separate node.
SamplerCustomAdvanced.why: Newer models (Flux, LTX) wire it this way so each part can be swapped. The small nodes feeding it are those parts.

BasicGuider.what: Bundles the model and the prompt into one guide for the custom sampler.

CFGGuider.what: Bundles the model with positive and negative prompts, and how strongly to follow them (CFG).

RandomNoise.what: The seed: the starting noise. The same seed with the same settings gives the same picture.
RandomNoise.why: Feeds Sampler Custom Advanced. Seed Hunt in the studio is trying many of these.

KSamplerSelect.what: Picks the sampling method (euler, dpm++ and so on).

BasicScheduler.what: Works out how much noise to remove at each step.
BasicScheduler.why: Its schedule (the sigmas) feeds Sampler Custom Advanced.

VAEDecode.what: Turns the finished latent back into a real picture you can see.
VAEDecode.why: It comes right after the sampler, because the sampler works in latent space and our eyes don't.

VAEDecodeTiled.what: VAE Decode in tiles, so big pictures and long videos fit in the graphics card's memory.
VAEDecodeTiled.why: After the sampler, like VAE Decode; used for large or long outputs.

VAEEncode.what: Turns a real picture into a latent so the sampler can work on it.
VAEEncode.why: Before the sampler, when you start from a photo or a frame instead of empty noise.

LoadImage.what: Brings in a picture from your computer.
LoadImage.why: Feeds anything that starts from a picture: an encode, a mask, a reference.

ImageScale.why: Usually right before saving, or before handing a picture to a step that needs a set size.

ImageUpscaleWithModel.what: Makes a picture bigger with an upscale model, adding real detail rather than just stretching.
ImageUpscaleWithModel.why: After decoding, once the picture is final.

UpscaleModelLoader.why: Its model goes to Upscale Image (using Model).

SaveImage.what: Saves the picture to the output folder.
SaveImage.why: The last stop. ComfyUI works backwards from save and preview nodes, so a chain without one never runs.

PreviewImage.what: Shows the picture without saving it.
PreviewImage.why: Also an ending node: it is why the steps before it run at all.

VHS_VideoCombine.what: Joins the frames into a video file, with sound if given.
VHS_VideoCombine.why: The last stop for video: frames in, finished file out.

VHS_LoadVideo.what: Brings in a video as a stack of frames.
VHS_LoadVideo.why: Feeds anything that works on existing footage: restyle, upscale, extend.

LongTakeTimeline.what: The plan of your long take: the beats, what happens when, and how many seconds each part lasts.
LongTakeTimeline.why: It feeds the Render node, which reads it to know what each chunk should show.

LongTakeCast.what: Who is in the take: each character's look and the pictures that keep them looking the same.
LongTakeCast.why: Feeds the Render node, so every chunk keeps the same faces and clothes.

LongTakeRender.what: The heart of a long take. It renders the film in short overlapping chunks, each starting from the end of the last, so they join into one unbroken shot. 'chunk 3/40' is this node counting.
LongTakeRender.why: It takes the Timeline, the Cast and the models, and runs a sampler inside every chunk, which is why you see the steps count up again for each chunk.

LongTakeAssemble.what: Stitches the chunks' latents into one take and decodes it.
LongTakeAssemble.why: After the Render node: the chunks are ready, and this joins the seams.

LongTakeMasterLook.what: Gives the whole take one look: colour, contrast and grain, the same in every chunk.
LongTakeMasterLook.why: Applied across the take so no chunk looks different from its neighbours.

LongTakeStudio.what: The studio's image editor as a node.
LongTakeStudio.why: Makes or fixes the opening picture that the long take starts from.

DPDLoadSplat.why: Feeds the 3D stage, so a camera can move through a real place.

DPDSongRangeMask.what: Marks which part of a song to repaint or extend.
DPDSongRangeMask.why: Feeds the music sampler, so only that stretch changes.

SetLatentNoiseMask.what: Tells the sampler which part of the latent it may change; the rest stays as it was.
SetLatentNoiseMask.why: Between the encode and the sampler, for inpainting: the mask decides where the new picture goes.

InpaintModelConditioning.what: Prepares an inpaint: the picture, the mask and the prompts, packed the way inpaint models expect.
InpaintModelConditioning.why: It sits before the sampler and hands it both the prompts and the starting latent.

LoadImageMask.what: Loads a black-and-white mask: white is where changes may happen.
LoadImageMask.why: Feeds anything that works on part of a picture.

ControlNetLoader.what: Loads a ControlNet: a guide that makes the picture follow a shape, a pose, edges or depth.
ControlNetLoader.why: Its ControlNet goes to an Apply ControlNet node.

ControlNetApplyAdvanced.what: Adds the ControlNet's guidance to your prompts, with how strong and over which steps.
ControlNetApplyAdvanced.why: It sits between the Text Encode nodes and the sampler, changing the prompts before they arrive.

CLIPVisionLoader.what: Loads a model that reads pictures the way CLIP reads words.
CLIPVisionLoader.why: Feeds CLIP Vision Encode, for workflows that take a picture as a prompt.

CLIPVisionEncode.what: Turns a picture into numbers that describe it, so a picture can guide the result like words do.
CLIPVisionEncode.why: Its output goes to a style or IP-Adapter node and from there to the sampler.

FluxGuidance.what: Sets how closely a Flux model follows your prompt.
FluxGuidance.why: Between the Text Encode node and the sampler: it adjusts the prompt numbers on the way through.

ModelSamplingFlux.what: Tunes how a Flux model removes noise, based on the picture size.
ModelSamplingFlux.why: Between the loader and the sampler: it adjusts the model before sampling.

ModelSamplingSD3.what: Tunes the noise schedule (shift) of SD3-style and many video models.
ModelSamplingSD3.why: Between the loader and the sampler: it adjusts the model before sampling.

LatentUpscale.what: Makes a latent bigger, for a second, sharper pass.
LatentUpscale.why: Between two samplers: the first draws small, the second adds detail at the larger size.

LatentUpscaleBy.what: Makes a latent bigger by a factor, for a second pass.
LatentUpscaleBy.why: Between two samplers, the same as Upscale Latent.

ImageScaleBy.what: Resizes a picture by a factor.
ImageScaleBy.why: After decoding, or before a step that needs a different size.

RepeatLatentBatch.what: Copies a latent several times, to make several pictures in one go.
RepeatLatentBatch.why: Between the latent and the sampler.

ImageBatch.why: Feeds nodes that work on several pictures at once.

EmptyHunyuanLatentVideo.what: A blank latent for a video: width, height and number of frames.
EmptyHunyuanLatentVideo.why: The video sampler's starting point, like Empty Latent Image for pictures.

EmptyLTXVLatentVideo.what: A blank latent for an LTX video.

CreateVideo.what: Joins frames into a video, with sound if given.
CreateVideo.why: After decoding, ready for Save Video.

SaveVideo.what: Saves the video to the output folder.
SaveVideo.why: An ending node: ComfyUI runs everything that leads into it.

SaveAnimatedWEBP.what: Saves frames as an animated WEBP.
SaveAnimatedWEBP.why: An ending node for short animations.

Note.what: A sticky note for people reading the workflow. ComfyUI skips it.
Note.why: It isn't wired to anything; it's there to explain.

MarkdownNote.what: A formatted note for people reading the workflow. ComfyUI skips it.
MarkdownNote.why: It isn't wired to anything; it's there to explain.

PrimitiveNode.what: Holds one value (a number, some text, a seed) that several nodes can share.
PrimitiveNode.why: Wire it into many inputs and change it in one place.

Reroute.what: A dot that bends a wire to keep the layout tidy. It changes nothing.

LongTakeRelayVSR.what: A fast 4x video upscale. Every 15 frames it draws one sharp keyframe in a single Wan step, and a tiny network carries that detail to the frames in between. Here it runs about 13 times faster than SeedVR2 with less flicker; SeedVR2 keeps faces a touch truer.
LongTakeRelayVSR.why: It comes last, after the video is decoded: upscaling only the finished frames is far cheaper than rendering big from the start. It frees the graphics card of every other model first, because it needs about 15 GB. Its counter is frames done.

LTXDirectorCS25.what: The Director: a timeline for one LTX 2.5 video. Prompts cut into segments over time, keyframes (first, middle and last frames), motion clips, sound and characters all sit on one track, and it turns them into what the sampler needs.
LTXDirectorCS25.why: It sits between the loaders and the sampler. It takes the model and text reader, and hands out a patched model, the prompts timed to each segment, the video and audio latents, and the guide data for the Director Guide.

LTXDirectorGuideCS25.what: Puts the Director's pictures and motion clips into the video: each keyframe is encoded and pinned to its frame, and motion clips steer the movement (IC-LoRA).
LTXDirectorGuideCS25.why: It comes right after the Director and before the sampler: it takes the Director's guide data and the prompts and latent, and hands the sampler the guided versions.

LTXDirectorCropGuidesCS25.what: Removes the extra guide frames that the Director Guide added to the end of the latent.
LTXDirectorCropGuidesCS25.why: It goes after the sampler, before decoding: the guide frames helped steer the video but aren't part of it, so they come off before you see it.

CleanLatentSliceCS25.what: Cuts a clean stretch of frames out of a video latent, from a start frame for a set length.
CleanLatentSliceCS25.why: Used after sampling to keep only the real frames, for example the clean_latent_frames count the Director reports.

LTXChunkWriterCS25.what: Writes one chunk of a long video out as picture frames and copies its last frames into ComfyUI's input folder, ready to be the first frames of the next chunk.
LTXChunkWriterCS25.why: It sits after decoding and passes the frames on unchanged, so a long video can be built chunk by chunk, each starting where the last one ended.

LTXChunkAssemblerCS25.what: Joins all the chunks of a run into one continuous picture sequence, cross-fading the overlapping frames.
LTXChunkAssemblerCS25.why: The last step of a chunked video: it writes straight to disk because a long video is far too big to hold in memory.

StubeliusLTXSetup.what: Decides how the seeds are rendered: full size, draft or low VRAM, how many seeds, and the speed-ups.
StubeliusLTXSetup.why: One of the Setup window's nodes: the Seeds and Finish nodes read their settings from it.

StubeliusLTXSeedSamplers.what: Picks a sampler for each seed, so the seeds can be rendered differently and compared.
StubeliusLTXSeedSamplers.why: Part of Setup: the Seeds node uses it for each version it renders.

StubeliusLTXModels.what: Loads everything LTX 2.5 needs in one place: the video model (safetensors or GGUF), LoRAs, the Gemma text encoder, the video and audio VAEs, the latent upscaler and memory options.
StubeliusLTXModels.why: The start of the chain: every other node in the workflow gets its models from here.

StubeliusLTXSeeds.what: Renders 1 to 4 versions of the video (seeds) at the first-pass size, each with its sound.
StubeliusLTXSeeds.why: It takes the Director's plan and the Setup's settings; you watch the versions side by side and pick a winner before spending time on the finish.

StubeliusLTXSeedPreviews.what: Plays every seed side by side, in sync, with sound: solo, A/B split or full size, and lets you pick the winner.
StubeliusLTXSeedPreviews.why: It shows what Seeds rendered, so only the winner goes on to the Finish.

StubeliusLTXFinish.what: Finishes the winning seed: an optional refine pass, the final resolution up to 4K, the final frame rate (RIFE) and the upscaler (RTX VSR or DLSS5).
StubeliusLTXFinish.why: The last stage: it only runs on the seed you picked, and reuses the cached seeds instead of rendering them again.

StubeliusLTXOutput.what: The finish settings and export: where the finished video goes and in what form.
StubeliusLTXOutput.why: Read by the Finish node; it sits in the Output window next to a split view for comparing.

StubeliusLTXTheme.what: Sets the colour theme of the workflow's windows.
StubeliusLTXTheme.why: Purely looks: it changes nothing in the video.

StubeliusLTXLivePreview.what: Shows the seeds and the finish while they are still being sampled.
StubeliusLTXLivePreview.why: A window onto the work in progress, so you can stop early if it's going wrong.

StubeliusLTXColorLock.what: Brings back the original colours after DLSS5 upscaling, which can shift them.
StubeliusLTXColorLock.why: It goes right after the DLSS5 upscale, comparing against the frames from before.

StubeliusLTXRIFEToFPS.what: Raises the frame rate with RIFE frame interpolation, keeping hard cuts clean instead of smearing across them.
StubeliusLTXRIFEToFPS.why: Part of the finish, after the video is decoded: more frames are drawn in between the ones that exist.

StubeliusLTXSeedHunt.what: The older way to try several seeds. Kept so old workflows still open; the Ultimate LTX Seeds node replaces it.
StubeliusLTXSeedHunt.why: Only in workflows made before the four-window version.

StubeliusLTXRefine.what: The older second-pass refine. Kept so old workflows still open; the Finish node's refine replaces it.
StubeliusLTXRefine.why: Only in workflows made before the four-window version.
